ORIGINAL USMLE-STYLE PRACTICE

After the paralytic lasts longer

A patient is intubated using a short-acting induction agent and rocuronium. Several minutes later the tube is secure, but continuing sedation has not been started. He remains immobile. Which next concern is most important?

  1. An inability to feel pain because the trachea is intubated
  2. Complete amnesia caused by rocuronium
  3. Awareness and pain despite persistent paralysis
  4. Proof that no further sedation will be needed
  5. Guaranteed absence of ventilator dyssynchrony after paralysis ends
Answer and explanation

Awareness and pain despite persistent paralysis

The induction effect may fade before neuromuscular blockade; continuing sedation and analgesia must be addressed.

Option explanations

Awareness and pain despite persistent paralysis: The induction effect may fade before neuromuscular blockade; continuing sedation and analgesia must be addressed.

Proof that no further sedation will be needed: Immobility does not establish unconsciousness.

Guaranteed absence of ventilator dyssynchrony after paralysis ends: Dyssynchrony may occur as blockade wears off.

An inability to feel pain because the trachea is intubated: Intubation does not abolish nociception.

Complete amnesia caused by rocuronium: Rocuronium does not provide amnesia.
